facts_for_explanation.what_it_is: A penalty because the employer's payroll report (Full Payment Submission) reached HMRC late, or a month with no payments wasn't reported. HMRC sends penalty notices every quarter.
facts_for_explanation.estimates: If reports are missing, HMRC may raise an estimated charge (a 'specified charge'). Only sending the missing report replaces it with the real amount.
facts_for_explanation.how_to_appeal: Online in HMRC's PAYE for employers service ('Appeal a penalty'), or by post to: National Insurance Contributions and Employers Office, HM Revenue and Customs, BX9 1BX. Quote the unique ID of each penalty from the notice. Usually within 30 days.
facts_for_explanation.pay: Paying within 30 days of the notice avoids interest.

appeal_output.signed_by: the business owner or a director
appeal_output.post_to: the address on the penalty notice
appeal_output.post_to_rule: Eduard 4 Nov 2026: use the HMRC address printed on the penalty notice (read from the letter); if it could not be read, tell the client to use the address on the notice.
appeal_output.known_address_to_check: National Insurance Contributions and Employers Office, HM Revenue and Customs, BX9 1BX
appeal_output.online_alternative: PAYE for employers → Appeal a penalty

inherits_note: Reasons, not-accepted list and routes come from the Self Assessment late filing rules (HMRC's reasonable excuse list is the same).

options.free: copy the wording and appeal online/by post
options.option2: £19 appeal letter emailed, client prints, signs, posts
options.option3: £39 accountant review: ID check; letter for the client to post AND appeal through the agent account (Eduard 4 Nov 2026, regardless of the deadline)
